text: Reacher knew the town was afraid before anyone told him.
People lowered their voices when certain names came up.
Worse than that.
The Duncans were a family, but they ran the town like a private kingdom.
They had money, muscle, and a long memory for anyone who crossed them.
Most people had learned to keep their heads down.
Reacher was bad at that.
That was answer enough.
The Duncans had built their power on fear.
Fear works well on people with homes, jobs, families, and something to lose.
Reacher was about to repossess it.
The first warning came in a parking lot.
Three men stepped out where Reacher could see them.
He liked when problems arranged themselves.
The biggest man did the talking.
He told Reacher he was in the wrong town.
He said the Duncans did not like strangers asking questions.
He said Reacher should move on while he still could.
Decided to make one of his own.
When it was done, the lot was quiet again.
One man sat against the truck, trying to remember how breathing worked.
"And tell them I did not like it.".
The Duncan house sat back from the road.
It looked strong from a distance.
It was a fort with curtains.
The men on the porch saw him before he reached the steps.
Reacher did not hide.
He wanted them watching him.
One man raised a hand and told him to stop.
He should have stayed inside.
The porch was clear.
Reacher stood in the yellow light and listened to the house.
Reacher entered anyway.
The Duncans expected begging.
They expected deals, threats, and shaking voices.
Every man there knew the night had turned.
The fight came in pieces.
One man rushed from the left and went down.
Another tried to circle behind him and found out Reacher had already counted him.
Two more came together, which only helped Reacher finish them closer to the same spot.
The room had fewer problems.
When it was over, the Duncans were finished.
Not just beaten.
It belonged to the people who had survived them.
